edit.description: Early soft control; redistribute ratio budget to later nodes; same M2 reward
edit.interpolation: smoothstep; phase is normalized over observed score nodes; no extrapolation
edit.normalization: dose is normalized over actual score nodes to a mean of one

failure_modes: The early-window landmark_00_local_dx/dy contrast is statistically indistinguishable between W1_early_soft and M2 across independent batches, falsifying H001.
Late-window dz values_z and node-to-node rates are unchanged between W1_early_soft and M2 within batch uncertainty, falsifying H002.
Mid-window soft_mass values_z are statistically indistinguishable between the dose recipe and M2 across independent batches, falsifying H003.

No decoded final affinity, survival or last recorded joint-head score is available, so any dose schedule cannot be credited with a measured affinity benefit; the primary affinity response must be assessed separately from strain and structural validity.

All read features have polynomial_accepted=false and high relative_node_RMSE, so no smooth trend or extrapolation beyond the observed window is supported; the recipe's phase knots are experimental hypotheses, not discovered stage boundaries.
Only 8 of 200 catalogue curve features were read; the remaining landmark displacement, covariance and soft-mass curves are unqueried, not absent, so the adopted feature set may be incomplete.
rationale: Adopt H001, H002 and H003, each backed by its delivered curve handles. The observed curves show non-monotone, sign-changing landmark_00_local_dx/dy displacement with the largest early-window excursions before t~0.15 (H001), late-window downward drift in landmark_00_local_dz and landmark_10_local_dz after positive early rates (H002), and early-rise/late-fall soft-mass at landmark_00 and landmark_10 (H003). All read features have polynomial_accepted=false, so these are observed-node descriptions over the score window [0.0,0.49] only. W1_early_soft is the registered dose recipe that lowers early dose (0.35) and raises late dose (1.65) with the same M2 reward, delta and blend, matching the observed early-excursion/late-drift structure; it is a testable hypothesis, not a discovered optimum. The dose lane preserves scalar geometry and only changes registered dose_factors, so no reward or curvature change is implied.
